title: Shipping Products When You Don't Know What they Can Do — Ben Stein, Teammates
talk_summary: A product manager at Teammates argues that because agent products are built on opaque LLMs with unbounded input surface area, PMs must shift from specifying features to specifying affordances, using evals as the new spec and vibe-coded prototypes to 'feel' the experience.

takeaways.technique: Evals as the product spec / merge gate
takeaways.what_they_do: Treat a written eval suite (LLM-judged criteria with a pass threshold) as the authoritative specification, so 'is this a bug?' is answered by the eval rather than by a prose spec or a reviewer's taste.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if the eval becomes the spec and we can say hey we said at you know 100% ... that is our metric
takeaways.numbers: cites 80% 'good enough' for some use cases and a 90% pass threshold as go/no-go

takeaways.technique: Probabilistic bug triage with explicit thresholds
takeaways.what_they_do: Distinguish deterministic bugs (must be 100%) from 'feel' issues, and only escalate the former to the backlog; use the eval threshold to decide feature-vs-bug instead of debating each case.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's like, oh, you know, closed, done, closed, duplicate. We need like closed LLMs be like crazy, yo

takeaways.technique: Adversarial 'QA walks into a bar' exploration
takeaways.what_they_do: Deliberately probe weird inputs and cross-tool combinations (LinkedIn comments, Spotify tracks) to discover emergent behavior rather than only testing specified cases.
takeaways.evidence_quote: QA engineer walks into a bar, orders a beer, orders two beers, orders zero beers, orders negative one beers, orders a lizard

takeaways.technique: Discover functionality by experimenting, not speccing
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of writing detailed requirements up front, ship building blocks and then explore what they can do, treating unexpected working behavior as a discovery to codify.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're actually building things and then discovering what they can do themselves. That sort of became the new job

takeaways.technique: Vibe-prototype to feel the interaction before speccing
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a throwaway prototype of the agent interaction to experience it (e.g. too many clarifying questions is annoying), explicitly not for production, purely to calibrate the spec.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's so easy to prototype and vibe code something and get the feels
